name: Political moderate
summary: A political moderate rejects radical or extreme views and seeks a position between the main poles, usually through compromise, gradual reform and attention to the merits of each issue. Moderation is a stance about method and range more than a fixed program, so moderates hold mixed positions that vary by country, and in practice they support democratic institutions, a mixed economy with a welfare state, and coalition-building across left and right.
scope: The generic political moderate: a stance of rejecting extreme or radical views and seeking compromise, gradual change and judgment case by case, as described by scholarship on moderation (de Haan and Lok), and by moderates' own accounts (Kabaservice). It excludes any particular party and the more programmatic strands, which have their own profiles (centrism, radical centrism, liberal centrism). Because the label is positional, many answers are low-confidence and stay null where the sources record no position.
